title: SDD — the binding
description: What sdd owns (SPEC §5): the signed design and the compiled scenarios bound to tests and interfaces per work item, before code. One document for the whole set, so an interface two items share is written once by one hand and named verbatim by both. The writer returns the items and its questions; the runner writes the id, the traces and the stamp. sdd never invents an interface: every control is the design's by id, every test proves a criterion by id.

traces.description: What the binding was written from, by hash: the pinned handoff and the intake record.

items.description: One binding per intake work item — a story, or a requirement no story carries. Not one per requirement: the work item is what gets built, and a binding that skips it breaks the chain a build walks back to the PRD.

questions.description: What the binding could not decide without guessing. A blocking question blocks the stage until a human answers in Discovery or overrides on the record; a guess written past would be invisible. Delivery cannot amend the PRD — the question crosses the seam as a question.

subject.description: The work item, criterion or screen the question is about, by id.

work_item.description: The intake work item this binds. Exactly one binding per work item is arithmetic.

approach.description: How it gets built, in prose — the first place mechanism may be discussed. Say what is exercised and where state lives; do not restate the story.

interfaces.description: The contracts this item exposes or consumes: functions, routes, events, files. An interface two items share is named here by both, `signature` character for character — the arithmetic compares them verbatim, and a disagreement is a build discovering it.

shared.description: True when another item names the same interface.

tests.description: One entry per thing the work item promises. Each names the criteria it proves by id — a join, so a criterion reworded later breaks nothing. `exercises` says what is run and `asserts` what is checked: a test that restates the criterion with a verb on the front names nothing to run and cannot come out either way.

proves.description: Criteria on this work item, by join id.

scenario.description: The compiled scenario this test implements (`STORY-n/m`), or null for a criterion no scenario carries.

level.description: Browser for a surface criterion: QA drives the product against the signed design.

controls.description: Every design control this item binds to, by the id the signed design gave it, on the screen the design holds it. Controls ⊂ design is arithmetic: an id the design does not carry is an interface nobody decided.

surface.description: The files this item expects to touch, as globs relative to the product repository. Overlap between items is expected and costs nothing; a surface that is wrong is what fails a build.

risks.description: What could make this binding wrong — a story that is infeasible or bundled belongs here and in a question, never designed around.
